text: Give the structural reason IPv6 deployment has taken thirty years.
choices: It is not backwards compatible, so adopting it alone reaches nothing new; NAT relieved the pressure; and the waist of the hourglass is the hardest thing to change
IPv4 addresses have not actually run out
explanation: There was never a moment when adopting IPv6 alone let you reach anything you could not already reach, so you had to run both — more work, no immediate benefit. A problem made survivable is a problem that does not get solved.
